sections.label: Age of building stock
sections.summary: About 70% of Singapore's building stock is more than 20 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Today, about 70% of our building stock is more than 20 years old.

sections.label: Consolidating building life-cycle requirements
sections.summary: The Bill aims to consolidate design, construction and maintenance requirements over a building's life-cycle under the Building Control Act by porting provisions from the BMSMA at clauses 21, 45 and 48.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: One of the key aims of this Bill is to consolidate the design, construction and maintenance requirements over a building's life-cycle under the Building Control Act, by porting over the relevant provisions from the BMSMA, at clauses 21, 45 and 48.

sections.label: Lift and escalator industry control
sections.summary: The Bill will strengthen regulatory control over the lift and escalator industry, allowing a Progressive Wage Model to be mandated for the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: First, it will strengthen regulatory control over the lift and escalator industry, allowing us to mandate a Progressive Wage Model for this sector.

sections.label: Number of lifts and escalators
sections.summary: There are about 70,000 lifts and 7,000 escalators in Singapore today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: So, let me go through these areas in turn.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: There are about 70,000 lifts and 7,000 escalators in Singapore today.

sections.label: Powers over errant contractors
sections.summary: Under new section 29R, BCA can disallow an errant L&E contractor from new jobs, cap new jobs, or mandate retraining to specified standards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under the new section 29R, BCA will also be able to disallow an errant L&E contractor from taking on new L&E jobs for a specified period, or cap the number of new L&E jobs that can be taken for a specified period, or mandate that employees are retrained to specified standards.

sections.label: Mandating PWM for lifts
sections.summary: Lift firms with 95% market share committed to the PWM, and under new section 29Q BCA can mandate PWM adoption as a registration requirement, aiming to do so by 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The results have been encouraging and lift firms representing 95% of the market share have committed to adopt the PWM.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Under the new section 29Q, BCA is conferred powers to mandate PWM adoption as a registration requirement for L&E firms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: We aim to mandate PWM for the lift industry by 2022.

sections.label: Falling facade element incidents
sections.summary: BCA received reports of almost 30 falling facade element incidents each year over the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Over the last three years, BCA received reports of almost 30 incidents involving falling facade elements each year.

sections.label: Facade inspection regime requirements
sections.summary: The regime covers buildings over 13 metres high and over 20 years old, with inspections by trained personnel every seven years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The regime will apply to buildings that are more than 13 metres high – or roughly four storeys – once they are over 20 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Inspections must be conducted by trained personnel every seven years.

sections.label: Accessible route upgrading limits
sections.summary: Accessible routes from ground floor entrances to lifts cannot be required without A&A works, so pre-1990 upgrading is voluntary, and amendments aim for holistic treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: However, we cannot require the building owner to provide an accessible route connecting the building entrance on the ground floor to the lifts if no A&A works are carried out there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Thus, for many buildings built before 1990, such basic accessibility upgrading is only carried out on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: We are amending this to make sure that we can provide a more holistic treatment.

sections.label: New section 22DA accessibility powers
sections.summary: Clause 17 introduces section 22DA empowering the Commissioner to require basic accessibility features during approved A&A works, applying to commercial and institutional buildings over 500 sqm GFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To accelerate accessibility upgrading in our existing buildings, especially the private ones, clause 17 introduces a new section 22DA that empowers the Commissioner of Building Control to require the owner of a building without basic accessibility features to provide these features when the owner or someone else undertaking A&A works to that building that requires plan submissions to BCA is given approval for those A&A works, regardless of where those A&A works are carried out in the building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The new section 22DA will apply only to commercial and institutional buildings with a gross floor area (GFA) of more than 500 sqm.

sections.label: Approved person accountability rules
sections.summary: Clauses 31 and 32 amend sections 29F and 29G so only a Director or Board member can be an approved person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To ensure proper accountability, clauses 31 and 32 amend sections 29F and 29G to stipulate that only a Director or a Board member can be an "approved person".

sections.label: Wider sanctions on builders
sections.summary: Clause 34 amends section 29J to widen the range of regulatory sanctions the Commissioner can impose on builders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Clause 34 amends section 29J to widen the range of regulatory sanctions that the Commissioner of Building Control can impose on builders.

sections.label: Welcome lift amendments
sections.summary: The amendments are welcome, especially given episodes of lifts breaking down in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments are certainly welcome, especially in light of episodes of lifts breaking down in 2018.

sections.label: Lift technician numbers
sections.summary: The Member asks how many lift technicians the industry currently has, noting the Minister of State mentioned 70,000 lifts in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share with this House how many lift technicians do we have in the industry currently?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister of State mentioned that there are 70,000 lifts in Singapore.

sections.label: Lift maintenance frequency review
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Minister would look into how maintenance frequency for lifts and mechanised carparks is determined.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would Minister look into how the frequency of maintenance for lifts and mechanised carparks is determined?

sections.label: HDB exterior feature responsibility
sections.summary: Clause 2(q) removes HDB as the person responsible for the exterior feature and places responsibility on the Town Council or its engaged contractor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By this Bill, clause 2(q) will amend the law to remove HDB as a person responsible for the exterior feature, and place the responsibility on the Town Council or a contractor engaged by the Town Council who has charge and control of the management and maintenance of common property.

sections.label: Defence for exterior feature defects
sections.summary: The Member notes the Minister's clarification on HDB paying rectification costs, and that proposed section 25H gives a defence if the defect was caused by supplied materials or work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: During the MND COS, I note that Minister had clarified that if an HDB block had a falling façade that could be attributed to a construction fault, HDB should pay the cost of rectification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In fact, the proposed section 25H makes clear that if a person responsible for an exterior feature can show that the defect was caused by materials or work supplied, the person responsible has a defence to a charge of failing to maintain the feature.

sections.label: Inspections by appropriate persons
sections.summary: The Bill removes the need for inspections and works to be overseen by qualified persons and requires them to be done by appropriate persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill will remove the need for such inspections and works to be overseen by qualified persons and simply require them to be done by appropriate persons.

sections.label: Access features for PWDs
sections.summary: New section 22DA lets the Commissioner of Building Control require building owners to erect features facilitating access and use by PWDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 22DA allows the Commissioner of Building Control to require building owners to erect features to facilitate the access to and use of a building by PWDs.

sections.label: PWM for lift industry
sections.summary: The amendments legislate the PWM for the lift industry, applying only to Singaporeans and PRs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the amendments will legislate the PWM for the lift industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I applaud the efforts to raise the wages of lift maintenance personnel who have to do a very difficult but an essential one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, the PWM will only apply to Singaporeans and PRs.

sections.label: Reviewing SS 550 lift lighting
sections.summary: The Lift and Escalator Sectoral Tripartite Committee recommended reviewing SS 550 to specify higher lighting levels within lift shafts for maintenance work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, the Lift and Escalator Sectoral Tripartite Committee has recommended reviewing the Singapore Standard SS 550, the Code of Practice for lifts, to specify higher lighting levels within the lift shaft to facilitate maintenance work.

sections.label: Facade inspection costs for Town Councils
sections.summary: The Bill requires facade inspection for buildings over 20 years old, then seven-year cyclical inspection, and asks who bears the costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, as mentioned in this Bill, there will be a requirement to conduct the facade inspection regime for buildings which are older than 20 years and, thereafter, conducting a seven years' cyclical inspection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A town like Aljunied-Hougang is home to many HDB blocks which are 20 years and above, approximately more than 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In view of this inevitable additional expenses, I would like to seek clarification from the Ministry whether the Town Councils will have to solely bear the additional expenses or will HDB, as the landlord, co-share the payment, which is similar to their current practice for facade repair expenses?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Additionally, will the Ministry consider additional funding for Town Councils?

sections.label: BCA study on technicians
sections.summary: Based on a BCA study, there are around 2,400 technicians, of which 42%, or slightly over 1,000, are residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As shared by the Minister of State, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, based on a study conducted by BCA, there are around 2,400 technicians of which 42%, or slightly over 1,000 are residents.

sections.label: Committee recommendations accepted by Government
sections.summary: Recommendations accepted by the Government on 19 September 2018 aim to provide better jobs, upskill the workforce, ensure commensurate wages and push technology adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: A set of recommendations was made by the Committee and accepted by the Government on 19 September 2018 to provide better jobs to attract Singapore residents to join the industry, upskill the workforce to deliver better quality maintenance services, ensure commensurate wages to build up a core workforce to anchor the industry and push for the wider adoption of technology to reduce manpower reliance.

sections.label: Lift industry wages and careers
sections.summary: New section 29Q lets the Commissioner of Building Control set minimum basic wage and bonus for lift industry workers after Tripartite Committee recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We need to attract young Singaporean to make them feel excited about the industry and their potential long-term career progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome the new section 29Q that gives the authority to the Commissioner of Building Control to specify the minimum amount of basic wage and bonus payable to the workers in the lift industry after considering the recommendations of the Tripartite Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Committee recommended that by 1 July 2022, all lift and escalator companies will pay the local technicians the salaries recommended by the Tripartite Committee.

sections.label: Mandatory monthly lift maintenance
sections.summary: The Building and Construction Authority currently requires lift owners to have monthly maintenance by an approved lift contractor for safe operation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, the Building and Construction Authority currently mandates that a lift owner shall subject the lift to monthly maintenance by an approved lift contractor to ensure safe operation of the lifts.

sections.label: Technology and lift maintenance procedures
sections.summary: Remote monitoring and diagnostics can notify technicians of faults and pre-empt breakdowns, and the passage asks if the Commissioner may vary maintenance procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: For example, remote monitoring can collect data from lifts and notify technicians of faults or irregularities while remote diagnostics can improve the trouble-shooting process and pre-empt breakdowns before they happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, under this Act, would the Commissioner of Building Control be given the mandate to exercise flexibility to vary the standard operating procedures for lift maintenance given the advancement in technology?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   I welcome the amendments in the Building Control Bill that gives the authority to the Commissioner of Building Control to specify the minimum amount of basic wage and bonus payable to the workers in the lift and escalator industry after considering the recommendations by the Progressive Wage Model recommendations by the Tripartite committee for this industry.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model and worker certification
sections.summary: The Progressive Wage Model links salaries to competencies, responsibilities and productivity, and maintenance workers must have minimum qualifications or certification before unsupervised work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model will ensure that their salaries commensurate with the competencies, responsibilities and productivity of the lift and escalator workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I look forward to working with the industry stakeholders to create a better and safe environment not only for our workers but the public as users as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I welcome the introduction of the requirement for elevator maintenance workers to possess minimum qualifications or certification before they can be allowed to perform works without supervision.

sections.label: Adequacy of lift parts
sections.summary: The passage asks how adequacy of lift parts can be ensured for the mandatory maintenance regime given existing lifts can only be replaced after 28 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, how could we ensure the adequacy of lift parts to meet the mandatory lift maintenance regime as prescribed here since the replacement of existing lifts can only be done after 28 years?

sections.label: Lift performance benchmark and retrofitting
sections.summary: The passage asks about a national lift performance benchmark like LTA's for MRT trains and supports empowering the Minister to order retrofitting of safety features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Do we have a national benchmark for lift performance similar to what LTA has done for MRT trains?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I fully support the amendment to empower the Minister to order existing lifts to be retrofitted with safety-related features.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for sector
sections.summary: Introducing the Progressive Wage Model to attract more Singaporeans to join this sector is a good start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Introducing the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to attract more Singaporeans to join this sector is a good start.

sections.label: Accessibility features for older buildings
sections.summary: Clause 17 targets pre-1990 buildings without basic accessibility features, applying to commercial and institutional buildings, with an Accessibility Fund co-funding up to 80% for residential and factory owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The changes under clause 17 target older buildings built before 1990, which do not have basic accessibility features.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are applying this requirement to commercial and institutional building types as these are more frequently accessed by members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Owners of residential and factory buildings can tap on the Accessibility Fund to co-fund up to 80% of the cost for installing basic accessibility features.

sections.label: HDB facade repair co-payment
sections.summary: Facade repair issues come under an existing HDB co-payment scheme, with HDB co-funding 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Also, to clarify on the co-payment by HDB should you have facade repair issues, that comes under an existing HDB co-payment scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I think the Member also knows that if it is found to be a facade repair issue, HDB co-funds 50%.

sections.label: Lift numbers and safety incidents
sections.summary: There are 70,000 lifts in Singapore, with fewer than 30 safety incidents from technical faults per year over the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the number of lifts in Singapore and their reliability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: There are 70,000 lifts in Singapore and the number of safety incidents arising from technical faults has been less than 30 per year over the last three years.

sections.label: Supervising engineers for lifts
sections.summary: There are about 90 SPEs whose primary duties include supervising lift installation and carrying out routine inspections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Today, there are about 90 SPEs whose primary duties include supervising the installation of lifts and carrying out routine inspections.

sections.label: Lift technicians with competency certificate
sections.summary: Almost 400 of the 2,100 lift technicians in Singapore have received the certificate of competency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: To date, almost 400 of the 2,100 lift technicians in Singapore have received the certificate of competency (CoC).

sections.label: Lift technician PWM wages
sections.summary: A lift technician at specialist level earns a basic wage of at least $2,250, while a master specialist could earn $4,000 or more monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, a lift technician with the specialist level of competency will be able to earn a basic wage of at least $2,250, while a master specialist could earn $4,000 or more a month.

sections.label: Certification for lift technicians
sections.summary: BCA will require all lift technicians, including foreigners, to be certified for PWM competency levels, and will encourage companies to apply other PWM principles to foreign technicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: BCA will require all lift technicians, including the foreigners, to be certified for the various competency levels in the PWM, and we will encourage lift companies to also incorporate other PWM principles for their foreign lift technicians as well.

sections.label: Clause 20 lift orders
sections.summary: Clause 20 lets the Commissioner of Building Control issue orders on lifts to prevent safety incidents, not to improve working conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: On Mr Zainal's specific point, I would like to clarify that clause 20 of the Bill allows the Commissioner of Building Control to issue orders in respect of lifts to prevent safety incidents and not to improve working conditions.

sections.label: Centralised lift parts storage
sections.summary: Timely rectification of lift faults is important, but centralised storage of lift parts from different manufacturers and models is neither practical nor cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We agree that it is important for lift faults to be rectified in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: However, having a centralised storage of the various lift parts from different manufacturers and across different models is neither practical nor cost-effective.

sections.label: Spare parts proprietary rights
sections.summary: The EU prohibits companies from restricting spare part sales, and Singapore has similar laws to deal with refusals to supply essential parts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Mr Zainal Sapari also raised concerns about major players exerting proprietary rights over their spare parts and asked if we could adopt the EU's practice of encouraging open and non-proprietary lift systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We understand that EU prohibits companies from restricting the sale of spare parts to other companies and we have similar laws in Singapore that can deal with refusals to supply essential parts.

sections.label: Mechanised car parking systems
sections.summary: There are about 260 MCPS in Singapore, and BCA will work out the MCPS regulatory regime details and consult the industry further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: On Mechanised Car Parking Systems (MCPS), we agree with Er Dr Lee that they should be properly installed and maintained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: There are about 260 MCPS today in Singapore, and 10 or less MCPS were installed annually in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But BCA will work out the details of the MCPS regulatory regime and consult the industry further on the requirements for contractors and technicians.

sections.label: Lift tenders and drone inspections
sections.summary: Each tender covers about 300 lifts, and Nee Soon Town Council uses drones for facade inspection, prompting a suggestion for MND and CAAS to address concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Each tender covers about 300 lifts, which is large by industry standards.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Nee Soon Town Council has been using drones to do facade inspection.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: So, I was wondering can MND work out with CAAS to address their concern so that we can be more productive?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: It is in our interest, in fact, to leverage more on technology and leverage more things like drones, for example, so that we minimise the cost to Town Councils to have to put up gondolas each time.

sections.label: Injured workers and lift retrofitting
sections.summary: Injured workers can claim under WICA, and with 70,000 lifts, the initial estimate for retrofitting existing lifts can be very expensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If they are injured, they can claim under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
sentences.text: My question is, given the fact that we have 70,000 lifts and we are trying to improve the working conditions, I think the initial estimate for retrofitting existing lifts can actually be very expensive.
